body_art_school: I started in art, with a foundation year in art and design in London, then a degree in painting and sculpture at Brighton. An MA in Applied Imagination at Central Saint Martins followed.
body_engineer: Moving from Japan to Silicon Valley, I found that code could be another kind of canvas. Engineering became an extension of my art practice, a way to make things that move and respond. I became a UI engineer at Apollo Group, then on contract at Apple, and at eBay’s Human Interface Group I built the loading spinner that went live on eBay.com.
body_mentoring: I mentor designers and engineers on ADPList, on their careers, their craft and finding their own way of making things. That’s $t(common:mentoring_sessions) sessions so far.
body_people: Then the work became about people. At Indeed I managed a design technology team of four, and at Rakuten Ready I helped launch its pickup service, working between product, design and engineering.
body_platforms: Now I build the tools other people make things with. Back at Apple, I lead design and engineering for Apple University’s platform, with a shared design system, a federated front end and an MCP server that lets people who don’t code turn an idea into a working prototype.
body_stores: At Apple Retail I built the Apple Watch demo that ran in Apple Stores worldwide, and shipped features and localized content to more than 30 locales at each product launch.
body_systems: At Tesla Energy, I led an engineering team globally responsible for the Solar platform. We cut outages from more than 20 a week to nearly zero.
body_web: The screen was my next medium. I designed brand sites, online shops and an iPhone app for Le Ciel Bleu in Kobe, then worked in Osaka as a web and product designer at Hasco.
lead: For me, engineering is a creative practice.
lead_material: Code is a material. Technology is a medium. And building something that didn’t exist before is still the most rewarding part.
